note: A primitive self-service campground in Land Between the Lakes on the east shore of Kentucky Lake, with gravel pads, a boat ramp and lake access. Only a few pads take a small RV. No water at the campground. --Claude
summary: Kept, lakefront kept. $10 a night per camping unit, self-pay, year-round, not on rec.gov, confirmed on LBL's self-service page. Imagery shows cleared pads at the shoreline tree line beside the boat ramp with open beach to the water (~15-30 m). Corrected the lake: Kentucky Lake (stored waterfront evidence says Lake Barkley).
flags: Waterfront lakefront kept: on Esri imagery the cleared pads around the boat ramp (around 36.7131,-88.0745, and the spur at ~36.7133,-88.0738) sit at the shoreline tree line with only open sand beach between them and the water, ~10-20 m to the tree/high-water line and ~30 m to the water in the image. LBL posts no site numbers or site map, so I cannot name sites; all sites are first-come self-pay, sold nightly. Kayak test passes (beach + ramp onto open Kentucky Lake). Most of the campground is under full canopy farther back.

Lake name: the stored waterfront_evidence says 'Lake Barkley shoreline' but the campground is on Kentucky Lake (Kenlake State Resort Park, 1552, is directly across on the W shore 9.8 km away); the note says Kentucky Lake. Suggest correcting the evidence text.

Potable water / hookups: the LBL page lists the amenities (pads, tables, grills, fire rings, vault toilets, trash, lake access, ramps) with no water or electric (only Fenton gets '30 amp electric'), consistent with the stored hookups 0/false and potable_water false (derived); left those groups as stored.
